s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a tender lytic lesion
salient_findings: Follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
key_facts: Man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
Swelling was slightly tender and increased in size over the month prior to presentation
Previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago
CT image showed a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
Residual right goiter was noted on imaging
The posterior aspect of the lesion was in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Pathological examination showed thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

differentials: Giant cell tumor of the bone
Thyroid metastasis from other primary sites
per_call: Giant cell tumor of the bone
Thyroid metastasis from other primary sites

shortlist.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion

shortlist.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Previous history of thyroid surgery and presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium

shortlist.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to follicular thyroid carcinoma, with potential for local invasion

shortlist.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, still a possible cause of a lytic lesion in the manubrium

shortlist.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but aggressive tumor that could explain rapid growth of the manubrial lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion and the goiter, along with the lytic lesion replacing the manubrium and the pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, are consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma, which is known for its potential to metastasize to bone and present with distant metastases.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma typically presents with lymph node metastases and has distinct nuclear features, which were not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Hürthle cell carcinoma is a variant of follicular thyroid carcinoma but the case does not specifically mention the presence of Hürthle cells.

rejected.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Medullary thyroid carcinoma originates from the parafollicular cells and would not be expected to show follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration.

rejected.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is a highly aggressive tumor that typically presents with a rapidly enlarging neck mass and has a poor prognosis, but the case does not describe such aggressive features or mention anaplastic cells on pathology.
